tagline: Leading Spain's energy transition through renewable capacity expansion and decarbonization
hero_kpi_rationale: Peninsular renewable capacity is Endesa's primary strategic growth driver, aligned with the European energy transition and the decarbonization of Spain's power mix.
company_description: Endesa, S.A. engages in the generation, distribution, and sale of electricity in Spain, Portugal, France, Germany, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Singapore, Italy, Morocco, and internationally. It generates electricity from various energy sources, such as hydroelectric, nuclear, thermal, wind, and solar. The company also offers advisory services and technology relating to energy, distributed generation, and energy demand management; deploys infrastructures for charging electric vehicles, vehicle-to-grid, and second-life services for batteries; develops integrated services for local administrations, such as public lighting, smart city development, energy services, and solutions for connectivity; and provides financial solutions for energy producers, as well as offers engineering and construction services for facilities related to the electricity business. As of December 31, 2025, it had an installed capacity of 22,616 MW; operated 321,843 km of distribution networks and transmission grids; and distributed electricity to 9,590 thousand customers and gas to 1,699 thousand customers. The company was formerly known as Empresa Nacional de Electricidad, S.A

kpis.name: Peninsular Renewable Installed Capacity
kpis.explanation: Total power output from operational renewable plants, primarily wind and solar.
kpis.description: Renewable capacity installed in Spain (peninsula) as of September 30, 2024. This increase reflects Endesa's continued investments in wind and solar, key components of its decarbonization strategy.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in renewable capacity despite a challenging macro environment.

kpis.name: Renewable Electricity Generation
kpis.explanation: Amount of electricity produced from renewable sources over the first 9 months.
kpis.description: Significant year-on-year increase in renewable generation over 9 months, driven by favorable weather conditions. This performance reflects improved wind and solar irradiation compared to 2023.
kpis.signal: Strong rebound in renewable output driven by wind and solar.

kpis.name: Consolidated Revenue
kpis.explanation: Consolidated revenue for the first 9 months of the year.
kpis.description: Revenue declined despite stable production, reflecting an unfavorable pricing environment for power producers in 2024.
kpis.signal: Revenue decline due to lower electricity prices and demand.

kpis.name: Operating EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Profit before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization.
kpis.description: EBITDA increased significantly due to efficient cost management and higher profitability from renewable generation, demonstrating operational resilience.
kpis.signal: Improved operational profitability despite revenue decline.

kpis.name: Consolidated Net Income
kpis.explanation: Net profit attributable to shareholders over 9 months.
kpis.description: Net income improved strongly despite lower revenues, reflecting enhanced efficiency and reduced financial expenses.
kpis.signal: Significant increase in net profit driven by operational discipline.

kpis.name: Net Financial Debt
kpis.explanation: Total financial debt minus available cash.
kpis.description: Net debt remained remarkably stable compared to year-end 2023, despite ongoing investments, reflecting balanced financial management.
kpis.signal: Stable net debt, indicating prudent financial management.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees as of September 30, 2024.
kpis.description: As of September 30, 2024, Endesa employed 8,943 people, down 1% from year-end 2023, reflecting workforce optimization and improved productivity.
kpis.signal: Slight headcount reduction, consistent with automation and efficiency gains.

kpis.name: Gross Fixed Asset Investments
kpis.explanation: Spending on tangible and intangible fixed assets over 9 months.
kpis.description: Gross investments decreased in 2024 compared to 2023, reflecting prioritization of key energy transition projects and improved capital allocation efficiency.
kpis.signal: Reduced investments, likely due to project prioritization.

kpis.name: Net Electricity Sales
kpis.explanation: Volume of electricity sold to end customers.
kpis.description: Electricity sales declined over 9 months compared to 2023, reflecting weaker demand conditions and increased competition in the liberalized market.
kpis.signal: Decline in electricity sales, indicating weaker demand or heightened competition.

kpis.name: Digital Customer Penetration Rate
kpis.explanation: Proportion of end customers using digital services.
kpis.description: 99% of end customers are digitalized, a level maintained since end-2023, demonstrating the success of digital transformation and strong customer engagement with digital channels.
kpis.signal: Near-total digitalization rate, a sign of successful transformation.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Total dividend paid per share over the fiscal year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Annual total: dividends paid + share buybacks.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends and buybacks (2021-2025) in billion EUR. Source: yfinance cashflow.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Portion of net income redistributed. >80% = potentially unsustainable.

kpis.name: Earnings Per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares during the fiscal year. Measures the company's ability to generate profit per share: basis for Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Exposure to electricity price regulation
risks.summary: Endesa is highly exposed to changes in electricity price regulation in Spain and Portugal, particularly through price-capping mechanisms and energy transition policies. Regulatory decisions directly affect market price formation and commercial margins.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk for an integrated power producer-distributor in Spain/Portugal. The document explicitly mentions the impact of regulation on market pricing and energy transition. Moderate language but structurally critical context. Stable trend but high categorical weight for the sector.

risks.title: Volatility in gas and crude oil prices
risks.summary: Gas and Brent prices remain volatile due to the geopolitical environment. Endesa is directly exposed to this volatility in its thermal generation costs and gas trading margins (43,320 GWh sold). Diversification of gas sources partially mitigates the risk.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in section 4.2 with detailed data. Moderately intense language but quantified impact (-42.5% electricity, -7.9% gas). Current trend downward but recognized geopolitical volatility. High weight for generation and trading.

risks.title: Energy transition and thermal asset obsolescence
risks.summary: Endesa must transform its generation portfolio toward renewable energy (9,993 MW renewables vs 21,440 MW total). The risk of thermal asset obsolescence is accelerating with climate policies. The transition requires massive investments (1,346 M€ in 9 months) and exposes the company to stranded asset risks.
risks.score_rationale: Major strategic risk, described as the 'main challenge' (section 3.3). High-intensity language ('phasing out fossil technologies'). Trend increasing with 90% of investments directed toward decarbonization. Categorically critical weight for the business model.

risks.title: Increased competition in electricity and gas retail
risks.summary: Endesa is losing market share in retail: -3.4% in electricity liberalized market customers and -2.5% in gas customers. Competition is intensifying in the liberalized Spanish and Portuguese segments, compressing commercial margins despite digitalization (99% digital customers).
risks.score_rationale: Implied in market data: loss of electricity customers (-3.4% liberalized, -2.7% total) and gas (-2.5%). Moderate language but clear negative trend. Medium-high weight for retail segment (56,455 GWh sold).

risks.title: Cybersecurity of critical infrastructure and digitalization
risks.summary: Accelerated digitalization of distribution networks (319,919 km) and customer services increases exposure to cyberattacks. Endesa relies on ICT systems to manage 12.6 million customers and critical infrastructure. Risks include service disruptions, customer data theft, and infrastructure sabotage.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in the 2024-2026 Sustainability Plan as a 'growth accelerator'. Moderately intense language but recognition of rising risk. Trend increasing with massive digitalization (99% digital customers, 21,676 charging points). High weight for critical infrastructure.

risks.title: Dependence on Enel Group and governance risks
risks.summary: Endesa is controlled by 70.1% by the Enel Group (via Enel Iberia), limiting decision-making autonomy. Energy transition and investment strategies are aligned with the parent company's priorities, creating potential conflicts of interest with minority shareholders.
risks.score_rationale: Enel holds 70.1% of capital via Enel Iberia. Stated factually in section 3.1. Neutral language but concentrated ownership structure. Stable trend but structurally important weight for strategic decisions.

risks.title: Climate and hydrological risks for generation
risks.summary: Endesa's hydroelectric production depends heavily on weather conditions and precipitation levels. Climate variations (droughts, floods) directly affect generation and margins. Climate change increases the unpredictability of hydropower resources.
risks.score_rationale: Implied in hydro generation volatility (+60% in 9M 2024 vs 2023). Moderate language but quantified impact on generation mix. Trend increasing with climate change. Medium weight for generation (45,742 GWh produced).

risks.title: Supply chain risks and cost inflation
risks.summary: Endesa relies on suppliers for renewable generation equipment, grid materials, and services. Inflation in construction and material costs (steel, semiconductors) impacts energy transition investments (1,346 M€ planned in 9M 2024).
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in Sustainability Plan (supply chain). Moderate language but context of energy and material inflation. Stable trend but medium weight for large capex (1,346 M€ in 9M). Renewable investments expose the company to cost volatility.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or its applications in the management report. Endesa does not position AI as a current strategic lever.
evidence: No reference to AI, machine learning, or advanced automation in the document.
Absence of AI-related KPIs or initiatives in business segments or projects.
Primary focus on physical energy transition (renewables, grid, electrification).

events.title: Endesa shares slip after power utility’s second-quarter earnings miss estimates
events.body: Investing.com - Madrid-listed shares in Endesa (BME:ELE) fell in early trading on Tuesday after the power group posted second-quarter earnings that fell short of expectations.
